newsitem.title: UK: BAE, VICKERS MERGER SEEN UNLIKELY.
newsitem.headline: BAE, VICKERS MERGER SEEN UNLIKELY.

text.p: A weekend newspaper report suggesting that British Aerospace wants to take over tank and Rolls-Royce luxury carmaker Vickers Plc was dismissed by industry sources and analysts on Monday.
BAe routinely declines to comment on takeover speculation.
But one well-placed industry source described the report on Monday as "poppycock".
The Independent on Sunday newspaper said Vickers was close to completing the sale of its medical systems division in a move which would pave the way to an agreed merger with British Aerospace.

BAe already has a marketing alliance with Vickers selling arms overseas and the two are also teamed together with Lockheed Martin in bidding for Tracer, the multi-billion joint Anglo-U.S. requirement for a new armoured reconnaisance vehicle.

But industry sources said it made no sense for BAe to want to diversify into making tanks, a move which would be at odds with its declared aim of seeking consolidation of the European defence industry.
Analysts say it would be more likely for Vickers to be taken over by another armoured vehicle manufacturer, such as its powerful compatriot GKN Plc.
